title: External Gear Pump
model_title: External Gear Pump (Foot-Mounted, with Relief Valve)

introduction.definition: An external gear pump uses two meshing gears turning in a close-fitting housing. Liquid is trapped in the spaces between the gear teeth and the casing, carried around the outside from suction to discharge, and forced out where the teeth mesh. Flow is nearly proportional to speed and almost independent of pressure.
applications: Lubricating oil and fuel oil transfer
Lube-oil systems on turbines and compressors
key_points: Volumetric efficiency falls as clearances wear and viscosity drops

classification.configuration: External gear, two shafts, gears supported between bearings (sleeve bushings)
classification.drive: One driven (drive) gear transmits torque to the idler through the tooth mesh

introduction.summary: Two meshing spur gears turn inside a close-fitting figure-8 housing. On the inlet side the teeth come out of mesh, opening volume that draws liquid in; the liquid is carried around the outside of each gear in the tooth spaces and is displaced into the outlet where the teeth re-mesh. Flow is nearly proportional to speed; pressure is set by the system, so over-pressure protection (relief valve) is essential.

what_to_look_for: As the teeth come out of mesh on the suction side, the expanding space draws liquid in.
Liquid is trapped between the teeth and the housing and carried around the outside of both gears.
On the discharge side the teeth mesh again and squeeze the liquid out.

steps.text: As the teeth come out of mesh on the suction side, the expanding space draws liquid in.
Liquid is trapped between the teeth and the housing and carried around the outside of both gears.
On the discharge side the teeth mesh again and squeeze the liquid out.
Bushings support the gear shafts and are lubricated by the pumped liquid.
The integral relief valve opens and recirculates flow if discharge pressure exceeds its setting.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Flow almost constant with pressure (slight fall from slip); power rises linearly with pressure; flow rises linearly with speed.

parts.name: Pump Body (Gear Housing)
parts.function: Forms the figure-8 gear chamber, the inlet and outlet ports and the mounting feet; its bore wall seals the tooth tips.
parts.material: Cast iron or ductile iron (general/oil service), cast steel, stainless steel (CF8M) for corrosive or food service.

parts.name: Front (End) Cover
parts.function: Closes the gear chamber and carries the front bushings; its inner face controls the gear end clearance.

parts.name: Rear (Seal-Side) Cover
parts.function: Closes the chamber on the drive side, carries the rear bushings and forms the seal chamber for the drive shaft.

parts.name: Sleeve Bushing – Front, Drive Shaft
parts.function: Radial support for the gear shafts on both sides of the gears.
parts.material: Bronze, carbon-graphite, silicon carbide or PTFE-lined steel depending on fluid lubricity and abrasives.

parts.name: Sleeve Bushing – Front, Idler Shaft
parts.function: Radial support for the gear shafts on both sides of the gears.
parts.material: Bronze, carbon-graphite, silicon carbide or PTFE-lined steel depending on fluid lubricity and abrasives.

parts.name: Sleeve Bushing – Rear, Drive Shaft
parts.function: Radial support for the gear shafts on both sides of the gears.
parts.material: Bronze, carbon-graphite, silicon carbide or PTFE-lined steel depending on fluid lubricity and abrasives.

parts.name: Sleeve Bushing – Rear, Idler Shaft
parts.function: Radial support for the gear shafts on both sides of the gears.
parts.material: Bronze, carbon-graphite, silicon carbide or PTFE-lined steel depending on fluid lubricity and abrasives.

parts.name: Drive Gear & Shaft
parts.function: Receives torque from the driver and drives the idler gear through the mesh; displaces liquid.
parts.material: Carburised/hardened alloy steel for oil service; stainless steel or nitrided steel for corrosive service.

parts.name: Idler (Driven) Gear & Shaft
parts.function: Meshes with the drive gear to form the second displacement path; rotates in the opposite direction.

parts.name: Mechanical Seal
parts.function: Seals the drive shaft where it leaves the pump.
parts.material: Carbon / SiC faces; stainless steel metal parts; elastomers per fluid.

parts.name: Seal Gland Plate
parts.function: Holds the stationary seat and closes the seal chamber.

parts.name: Relief Valve Body
parts.function: Houses the relief poppet and connects the discharge side to suction to limit maximum pressure.

parts.name: Relief Valve Poppet
parts.function: Seals on the seat until discharge pressure overcomes spring force, then opens to bypass flow to suction.

parts.name: Relief Valve Spring
parts.function: Sets the cracking pressure of the relief valve.
parts.material: Spring steel or stainless spring steel.

parts.name: Adjusting Screw & Lock Nut
parts.function: Adjusts spring compression (set pressure); lock nut fixes the setting.

parts.name: Valve Cap
parts.function: Covers the adjusting screw and prevents tampering/leakage.

selection_notes: Reduce speed as viscosity rises to avoid cavitation in the tooth spaces.
Use hardened gears and bushings for poor-lubricity liquids.

alignment: Coupling alignment as for centrifugal pumps.
piping: Size the suction line for low velocity (viscous liquids need large suction pipes); provide a strainer.
Fit a pressure-relief valve (integral or in the discharge line) — a positive-displacement pump will build pressure until something breaks if the discharge is blocked.
Support piping independently of the pump.
commissioning: Never start against a closed discharge valve.
Fill the pump with liquid (or ensure the suction is flooded) before start — avoid dry running unless the design allows it.

overhaul.task: Measure gear end and tip clearances and bushing wear.

lubrication: Internal bushings lubricated by the pumped liquid.

causes: Too high speed for the viscosity
Setting too close to operating pressure

script.narration: This module introduces the External Gear Pump.
An external gear pump uses two meshing gears turning in a close-fitting housing.
Liquid is trapped in the spaces between the gear teeth and the casing, carried around the outside from suction to discharge, and forced out where the teeth mesh.
Flow is nearly proportional to speed and almost independent of pressure.

script.narration: How the External Gear Pump works.
As the teeth come out of mesh on the suction side, the expanding space draws liquid in.
Liquid is trapped between the teeth and the housing and carried around the outside of both gears.
On the discharge side the teeth mesh again and squeeze the liquid out.
Bushings support the gear shafts and are lubricated by the pumped liquid.
The integral relief valve opens and recirculates flow if discharge pressure exceeds its setting.

video_tutorials.title: External Gear Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the External Gear Pump.
Check discharge pressure and noise.
Check the shaft seal.
Verify relief-valve setting.
Measure gear end and tip clearances and bushing wear.
Watch for loss of flow (slip): lower flow at pressure. Common cause: worn clearances.
Watch for cavitation noise: whining, rattling. Common cause: too high speed for the viscosity.
Watch for relief valve chatter: noise, flow loss. Common cause: setting too close to operating pressure.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
